action_criteria.expected_evidence: Homogeneously enhancing right frontal periventricular mass with subependymal spread and corpus callosum involvement, no central necrosis, diffuse restricted diffusion, moderate edema and 6 mm leftward midline shift, single lesion
action_criteria.label: Order MRI brain with and without gadolinium contrast (tumor protocol with DWI, FLAIR, post-contrast T1) to characterize the right frontal periventricular lesion, define mass effect, and plan the biopsy
action_criteria.rationale: Contrast MRI with diffusion characterizes the lesion pattern (enhancement, necrosis, diffusion), excludes additional lesions, defines the mass effect that governs lumbar puncture safety, and plans the stereotactic target (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Moderately elevated rCBV (maximum ratio 2.4) with homogeneous distribution and no focal hot spot
action_criteria.label: Order MR perfusion imaging (DSC perfusion) to assess the vascularity of the mass and guide the biopsy target
action_criteria.rationale: Perfusion characterizes the vascularity of the enhancing mass and helps target the biopsy; a moderate, homogeneous rCBV elevation is lower than usually seen in glioblastoma.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Markedly elevated choline with marked NAA reduction and prominent lipid-lactate peaks; no 2-hydroxyglutarate peak
action_criteria.label: Order MR spectroscopy (1H-MRS) to characterize tumor metabolic profile
action_criteria.rationale: Spectroscopy supports a highly cellular neoplasm before biopsy; it does not establish the entity.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Mildly enlarged axillary lymph nodes with preserved fatty hila and mild splenomegaly, with no extracranial mass or bulky lymphadenopathy
action_criteria.label: Order contrast CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis to look for systemic lymphoma or another primary, given the palpable lymphadenopathy, and to stage a lymphoma
action_criteria.rationale: Body imaging distinguishes primary CNS lymphoma from secondary CNS involvement by systemic lymphoma and is part of standard lymphoma staging (IPCG; EANO PCNSL 2015); generalized lymphadenopathy is present on examination.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Leukopenia (3.4), lymphopenia (0.6), mild anemia and platelets 148 with normal PT, INR and aPTT and a negative antibody screen: no contraindication to stereotactic biopsy
action_criteria.label: Order pre-operative laboratory workup: CBC, basic metabolic panel, coagulation studies (PT/INR, aPTT), and type and screen before stereotactic biopsy
action_criteria.rationale: Platelets, coagulation and blood group must be known before a neurosurgical procedure.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: HIV-1 infection with viral load 156,000 copies/mL and CD4 82 cells/mcL (AIDS); Toxoplasma IgG positive, IgM negative
action_criteria.label: Order HIV testing with CD4 count and viral load, and toxoplasma serology, given weight loss, fevers, oral thrush, generalized lymphadenopathy and high-risk exposure
action_criteria.rationale: HIV status and the CD4 count define the differential of a brain mass (lymphoma, toxoplasmosis, other opportunistic infection) and change management; the accepted diagnosis depends on it (EANO PCNSL 2015).

action_criteria.label: Assess performance status (KPS and ECOG) at this visit
action_criteria.rationale: Performance status is a prognostic factor in primary CNS lymphoma and governs fitness for high-dose methotrexate-based induction (EANO PCNSL 2015).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, CD20 positive and EBER ISH positive (EBV-associated), non-germinal centre phenotype, Ki-67 above 90%, GFAP and IDH1 R132H negative
action_criteria.label: Obtain tissue by stereotactic biopsy of the right frontal periventricular lesion, with CD20 immunohistochemistry and EBER in situ hybridisation; resection is not the approach because the lesion is deep, periventricular and callosal and lymphoma is suspected, where resection brings no benefit
action_criteria.rationale: Stereotactic biopsy is the diagnostic procedure for suspected CNS lymphoma (EANO PCNSL 2015). Only tissue establishes the entity; CD20 and EBER define an EBV-positive B-cell lymphoma.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Methotrexate interacts with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and proton pump inhibitors; an unboosted antiretroviral regimen avoids most chemotherapy interactions
action_criteria.label: Check interactions between high-dose methotrexate, Pneumocystis and toxoplasma prophylaxis, antiretroviral therapy and corticosteroids
action_criteria.rationale: Induction, prophylaxis and antiretroviral therapy will start together; the interactions change the choice of prophylaxis around methotrexate cycles.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not perform a lumbar puncture while the 6 mm midline shift and papilledema persist: the pressure gradient risks herniation.
Do not initiate tumor-directed therapy (radiotherapy or chemotherapy) before tissue diagnosis is established.
Do not start therapeutic anticoagulation without a clear thromboembolic indication, given the upcoming neurosurgical procedure and bleeding risk.
Do not attempt resection of the lesion: in suspected CNS lymphoma, stereotactic biopsy is the diagnostic procedure and resection brings no benefit.
Do not start prophylactic antiseizure medication: the patient has had no seizure, and AIOM recommends against prophylaxis in brain tumour patients without a seizure history.
required_recommendations: Refer urgently to neurosurgery for stereotactic biopsy of the right frontal periventricular lesion, not resection, because the lesion is deep and callosal and lymphoma is suspected; send the specimen for histology with CD20 immunohistochemistry and EBER in situ hybridisation.
Withhold corticosteroids until the stereotactic biopsy is obtained, because they can render lymphoma non-diagnostic; give dexamethasone first only if herniation is impending [EANO_PCNSL_2015].
Obtain HIV testing with CD4 count and viral load, and toxoplasma serology, given weight loss, fevers, oral thrush and generalized lymphadenopathy.

Start Pneumocystis and toxoplasma prophylaxis with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (CD4 82 cells/mcL, Toxoplasma IgG positive), and replace it with atovaquone around high-dose methotrexate cycles because trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole increases methotrexate toxicity.

Complete lymphoma staging: slit-lamp ophthalmological examination for vitreoretinal involvement, contrast CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis (or PET-CT) and bone marrow biopsy; obtain CSF cytology and flow cytometry only once the mass effect has resolved.
Refer to haematology and neuro-oncology for high-dose methotrexate-based induction, and start antiretroviral therapy with infectious-disease input [EANO_PCNSL_2015].

metadata.diagnostic_challenge: Primary CNS lymphoma in an undiagnosed HIV/AIDS patient, initially referred as 'likely GBM.' Requires recognition of (1) clinical features of undiagnosed HIV, (2) imaging features distinguishing PCNSL from GBM (homogeneous vs ring enhancement, moderate vs high rCBV), and (3) fundamentally different management (chemotherapy, not surgery). Corticosteroids must be avoided before tissue diagnosis.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: Off-pathway tumor histology (primary CNS lymphoma rather than glioma); 4 required criteria (MRI, pre-operative labs, HIV testing, stereotactic biopsy), 2 red herrings; diagnosis requires recognizing the lymphoma imaging pattern, testing for HIV and withholding steroids before biopsy

patient.history_present_illness: 56-year-old right-handed African American male presenting with 3-week progressive headache, difficulty concentrating, personality change (more withdrawn and flat), and mild left arm clumsiness. He was initially evaluated at an outside hospital where a CT head revealed a right frontal mass with surrounding edema, and he was transferred for neurosurgical evaluation. He was referred with a preliminary diagnosis of 'brain tumor, likely GBM.' On further history, he reports 8 kg weight loss over 4 months, intermittent fevers (not measured at home), and night sweats. He admits to a 15-year history of unprotected sex with multiple male partners. He has not seen a doctor in over 10 years and has never been tested for HIV. On physical examination, oral thrush is noted and generalized lymphadenopathy is palpable.
